title: Refrigerator, freezer and wine cooler

parts.label: Refrigerator
parts.looks: The tall unit with fresh-food and freezer sections.
parts.normal: Fresh food at about 37 to 40°F and the freezer at 0°F on an appliance thermometer; a quiet hum that cycles on and off.
parts.abnormal: Warm food, sweating walls, or a running sound that never stops or never starts.

parts.label: Freezer
parts.looks: The freezer drawer, door or chest.
parts.normal: At or below 0°F with light frost at most.
parts.abnormal: Soft ice cream, or a thick sheet of frost on the back wall.

parts.label: Wine cooler
parts.looks: A short glass-door unit with wine racks, built in under a counter or free-standing.
parts.normal: Holds its set temperature; vents at the front or back are clear.
parts.abnormal: Warm, frosted, or the fan never runs.

parts.label: Door seal
parts.looks: The rubber strip around each door's edge.
parts.abnormal: Torn, flattened, or a gap where a strip of paper slides out easily with the door closed.

parts.label: Condenser coils
parts.looks: The black grid or coil behind the bottom front grille or on the back of the unit.

parts.label: Freezer back panel
parts.looks: The back wall inside the freezer, with the air vents.
parts.normal: Light frost at most; vents clear.
parts.abnormal: A thick even sheet of frost or ice over the panel and vents.

parts.label: Ice maker
parts.looks: The tray and arm in the top of the freezer.
parts.abnormal: Arm up (switched off), empty bin, or ice jammed in the chute.

faults.name: Dirty condenser coils
faults.evidence: Matted dust on the coils with a warm-running unit.

faults.name: Leaking door seal
faults.evidence: A torn or flattened seal, or a gap at the door edge; frost or sweat near that spot.

faults.name: Defrost system failure
faults.evidence: A thick even sheet of frost over the freezer's back panel and vents, with the fresh-food side warming up. The technician confirms which part.

faults.name: Blocked air vent between freezer and fridge
faults.evidence: Freezer cold but fresh food warm, with food or ice blocking the vents.

faults.name: Clogged defrost drain (water under the crisper drawers)
faults.evidence: Water pooling under the drawers or ice at the bottom of the freezer back wall.

faults.name: Compressor start relay or fan fault
faults.evidence: Clicking every few minutes from the back with the unit warm, or a condenser fan that never turns. The technician confirms.

faults.name: Wine cooler at its limit
faults.evidence: A thermoelectric (fan-only, no compressor) cooler in a hot room cannot cool far below room temperature; check the room and the vents first.

hazards.label: Water reaching electrics
hazards.threshold: Water on the floor from the fridge or ice maker visibly touching an outlet, a power strip or a cord.

may: Put an appliance thermometer in the middle of each section and read it after a few hours.
Close the door on a strip of paper and pull it to test the seal.
Pull the bottom front grille off and show the coils with the unit unplugged.
Clear food away from the vents.
must_not: Chip or pry at ice with a knife or sharp tool.
Open the back panel or touch the compressor wiring.

tour.open: Open the fridge and show me the inside from about a metre back.

checkpoints.hint: Open the freezer and point at its back wall.
Run the camera slowly along the door seal.
Show me the grille at the bottom front, or the back of the unit. Tap Light if it is dark.
